steps.text: Water can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas — but it's always H₂O. Let's move it between states.
Heat the ice to melt it into liquid water (melting), then heat it more to boil it into steam (boiling).
Cool the steam and it condenses back to water; cool the water and it freezes back to ice.
Solid, liquid, gas — all three are the same substance, H₂O. Adding or removing heat just changes its state.

coach.mission: Move water between solid, liquid, and gas.
whenStuck: Add heat to go solid → liquid → gas; remove heat to go back.
Watch the labels change: melting, boiling, condensing, freezing.
whenWrong: Heating melts then boils; cooling condenses then freezes.
It's the same water throughout — only the state changes.
whenCorrect: Right — heat changed the state of the water.
Good — all three states are still H₂O.
coach.done: You've moved water through all three states. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
